translations.text: they grew up huge, like giants: that was the worse offspring, descended from Cain. Then the men began to buy wives from one another:
by this Seth's kin was soon corrupted. The people of men became mixed with wickedness, and the children of men became a people hateful to him who created this light,
except that one of them had a nobleman's mind, a thane's way of thinking. He was an excellent man, wise and skilled in speech, and he had great understanding: he was called Enoch.
He became famous among men here on earth, throughout this middle world, because the best of kings [took] him from here still alive, living in his body,
so that he never died in this light. Instead, the ruler of heaven fetched him from here and set him there,
where he may always be in joy, until heaven's guardian sends him back into this world to the children of men, as a teacher for the people.

Then the hateful one will also come here: Antichrist will lead the whole nation, the whole host, astray. Then with a weapon, with sharp edges, by the strength of his hand, he will become Enoch's slayer;
the soul, the spirit, will turn onto the good way. Then God's angel will come and avenge him on the evildoer with the edges of weapons: Antichrist will be robbed of life, the fiend struck down.
The people, the companies of men, will be turned back to God's kingdom for a long while, and afterwards this land will stand safe for them.

Then the people of Sodom, the men, had sinned so badly that our ruler, the mighty Lord, was angry with them, because they practised wickedness and committed crimes. The children of fiends had taught them so much evil:
then the ruling God, the lord, would not put up with it. He commanded three, his angels, to go from the east on his errand and journey to Sodom, and he himself was there with them.

When the mighty ones travelled over Mamre, they found Abraham standing by a temple, keeping watch over a holy place. The best of men was to perform our ruler's sacrifice and to serve God there at midday.
When he saw them coming, he recognized God's power. He went to meet them and bowed down to God himself. He bent low and prayed, and asked earnestly that he might keep his favour from then on:
"Where do you wish to go now, ruler, my lord, almighty father?
I am your own servant, loyal and obedient. You are so good a lord to me, so generous with treasures: Lord, do you wish to have anything of mine? Lo!
It all rests on your judgement. I live by what you have granted me, and I believe in you, my good lord. May I ask you now, Lord of victory, where you wish to journey?"
Then God's answer came back to him, mighty words: "I will not keep it from you now," he said, "or hide from a loyal man where my mind is set.
We are to travel south from here: the men around the land of Sodom have sinned so badly.

Now the guardians cry out to me day and night. They recount their deeds and tell of their sins. Now I want to find out for myself whether those men commit such wickedness among themselves, such evil deeds.

If so, raging fire shall fall upon them, and their grievous crimes and sins shall sink them. Sulphur will fall from heaven with fire, and the wicked will die, the men of evil deeds, just as morning comes."
Then Abraham spoke (he had good courage and wise words), and he addressed his ruler: "Lo!
There was a throng of fiends there, hostile creatures, who had led the people astray into that wickedness. The reward was then at hand, great and deadly, for their having so often committed crimes.

There sat within the city a man of noble birth, Lot, among the people, who often worked the praise of God in this world. He had there plenty of wealth, goods he had gained. He was worthy in God's sight.
He was of Abraham's noble kin, his brother's child. There was no better man, with manly virtues, around the shores of the Jordan; he was endowed with wisdom. Our Ruler was gracious to him.
When the white sun sank to its seat, the brightest of all beacons, he stood before the city's gate.
Then in the evening he saw two angels walking into the dwellings, as they came from God, endowed with wisdom. At once he spoke to them with his words.
He went toward them and thanked God, heaven's king, for granting him the help that he might look upon them with his eyes,
and he kissed them on the knee and courteously asked them to visit his dwelling. He said that he would give them their own choice of whatever goods God had granted him in the land.
They were not at all too slow, but went into his guest-hall, and he served them devoutly. They told him many true words.
There he sat in watch, and kept his Lord's messengers, God's angels, in holiness. They told him so much that was good and true.
The dark, narrow night glided on into the clouds; morning drew near to every dwelling. The dawn-bird sang before the day's glory.
Then our Lord's messengers had found out the crimes that men committed around the city of Sodom.
Then they told Lot that a great slaughter of the children of men must come upon the people there, and likewise upon the land.
They told him to make ready and to go away from there, to remove himself from the fiends and to lead his wife with him, the nobly born woman.
He had no more of his kin there except his two daughters. With them, they commanded, he was to be up on a mountain before day, so that the burning fire would not catch him.

When he had hastily made ready for the journey, the angels, the messengers of heaven's king, set off. They held him by the hands, led him and instructed him for a long while, until they had brought him out beyond the city.
They commanded that, however great a crash they heard, a breaking in the cities, they must never look behind them, if they wished to live in the land.
Then the holy guardians, God's angels, turned back again, went swiftly, and journeyed to Sodom.
From there Lot travelled southward, following their instruction, and fled the throng of the people, of wicked men. Then day had come.

Then a great crash arose there, reaching to heaven; it burst and cracked. Every one of the cities was filled with smoke, so much fire had fallen there from the sky. There was an outcry of the doomed, of the hateful people.

Flame seized all the broad city-settlements. Everything burned together, stone and earth, and so many hostile men died and sank. Burning sulphur surged through the dwellings; the outlaws suffered a hateful reward.
The land sank in, the earth into the abyss. All the realm of Sodom was destroyed, so that not a single man survived, and it was deadened into a Dead Sea, as it still stands today, filled with water.
Then all the people of Sodom had paid dearly for their crimes, except that the Ruler, by his will, had led one of them out of there, and the women with him: three with the thane.

Then they heard the death-agony of the people, the cities burning. Then a nobly born woman looked back behind her: she would not carry out the teaching of the angels (that was Lot's wife), for as long as she was allowed to live in that land.
When she stood on the hill and looked back behind her, she was turned to stone. There she shall stand as a famous sign to men across middle-earth, from now on forever, as long as this earth lives.
